races.title: U.S. House, District 7
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Rebecca Bennett

money.note: Individuals gave $7,664,973; PAC money $520,754; candidate's own money $327. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and experimental test pilot who served more than 15 years in uniform, including in the Air National Guard. Cornell graduate with a Wharton MBA. Healthcare executive, most recently vice president at Oshi Health. Has not held elected office. Lives in Bridgewater, NJ.

endorsements.text: VoteVets, New Politics, Moms Demand Action (Gun Sense Candidate distinction), CWA District 1, NJ FMBA and several county Democratic committees, per her Ballotpedia survey.
Philadelphia Inquirer editorial board endorsement (Oct. 22, 2026), listed on her campaign site.
USA TODAY Network New Jersey editorial board (NorthJersey.com) and My Central Jersey editorial board endorsements, listed on her campaign site.
Former Republican Rep. Adam Kinzinger and the New Jersey State Association of Pipe Trades, per campaign press releases listed on her site.

cands.gaps: Her exact birthplace was not found; sources give only her birth date and say she was raised in Granbury, Texas. The 2019 move to New Jersey comes from a single source, Wikipedia. She has never held office, so there is no record of official actions. We found no statements from her on data centers, property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land use, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, or school choice and teacher pay. Her housing pledge (cut red tape, increase supply) was not scored against any position because it was too general. Her campaign site, which we used for her stated positions, shows what she says she will do, not what she has done.

qual.why: Executive and management experience in healthcare and military command leadership put her in the middle range. She has no legislative, budget-office or other governing record, which keeps the score from going higher.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she will pass gun safety reforms, get "weapons of war" off the streets and reimplement the tax on silencers.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says she will restore a woman's right to choose at the federal level.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she will support law enforcement officers' work and make sure local agencies have the resources and tools they need.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign site says the campaign is powered by people, not billionaires, lobbyists or corporate special interests, and it lists passing campaign finance reform among her goals.

money.note: Individuals gave $2,791,280; PAC money $1,463,215; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for New Jersey's 7th District since 2023. Earlier served in the NJ General Assembly (2001–03) and State Senate (2003–22), including as Senate Republican leader from 2008. Began his career at the EPA and as an aide to Rep. Bob Franks; volunteer firefighter and EMT.

controversies.text: Federal records show $20,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $351,871 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate; 1 staff trip paid for by that foundation.

This Congress, Kean missed 146 of 676 House votes (21.6%) through Sept. 16, 2026, including 142 in a row from March 17 to June 29, 2026. He said the absence was for a health issue that put him in the hospital.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by Donald Trump in the 2026 race.
Endorsed by Humane World Action Fund in the 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stances from Kean on data centers or new development, and nothing on limits for institutional or out-of-state home buyers. We also found no records on H-1B visas or immigration enforcement bills, red-flag laws or other gun measures, or police pay and pensions. The pages read gave no dates for his abortion votes. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through its list of key votes. His own account of his 2026 absence comes from secondhand reporting; we did not read his statement directly.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His 2020 campaign site said he was 'a leading driver of the 2% cap on municipal spending that helped stabilize property taxes' and that he would prioritize fiscal responsibility.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign biography cites a 'student-focused approach to education initiatives, such as expanding school choice' during his time as a legislator.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His 2020 campaign site said he built a reputation as an advocate for open space and conservation in the legislature and passed laws to ensure open space and conservation are well funded.

pro-life.evidence: Voted against the Women's Health Protection Act, which would have codified abortion rights overturned by the Supreme Court (date not given in the page read).
